standards.note: Thailand Surface Water Quality Standard (PCD) & WHO drinking-water guideline: Arsenic (As) ≤ 0.010 mg/L.

caveats: Official open-data station CSVs currently cover 23 stations across Chiang Rai's Kok, Sai, Ruak, Mekong and control tributaries (8 rounds). Values reported as '<0.010' are below detection limit (plotted at 0.005 mg/L in trends and counted as compliant); '0' indicates a station was not sampled in that round. Separate PCD press briefings in late 2026 reported flood-season spikes up to 0.284 mg/L in the Sai River. National watchpoints (Mae Ai KK01–03, Salween, Ron Phibun, Chatree, Ban Rai) are context markers without a unified national CSV.

summary.pcd_flood_peak_note: Up to 0.284 mg/L (~28× standard) reported by PCD in Sai River flood peaks (2026).

watchpoints.th_name: แม่น้ำกก ชายแดน ต.ท่าตอน อ.แม่อาย
watchpoints.summary: Upstream entry of the Kok River from Shan State, Myanmar; repeated PCD surface-water & sediment As exceedances; proposed head of Thailand's ~150 km Kok Pollution Control Zone.

watchpoints.th_name: ลุ่มน้ำสาละวิน จ.แม่ฮ่องสอน
watchpoints.summary: Monitored by PCD / REO1 for transboundary arsenic & heavy-metal runoff from upstream mining in Shan & Kayah States, Myanmar.

watchpoints.name: Ron Phibun Historic Arsenic Zone
watchpoints.th_name: อ.ร่อนพิบูลย์ จ.นครศรีธรรมราช
watchpoints.summary: Thailand's landmark chronic arsenic poisoning site ('Black Fever' / โรคไข้ดำ since 1987) linked to arsenopyrite leaching from legacy tin & tungsten mines into shallow groundwater.

watchpoints.name: Chatree Gold Mine Belt (Phichit–Phetchabun)
watchpoints.th_name: พื้นที่รอบเหมืองแร่ทองคำชาตรี (พิจิตร–เพชรบูรณ์)

watchpoints.name: Ban Rai Geological Arsenic Study Area
watchpoints.th_name: อ.บ้านไร่ จ.อุทัยธานี
